reference.description: Assembled byte by byte: BITMAPINFOHEADER, uncompressed 24-bit BGR, bottom-up rows (the first stored row is the bottom one) and three padding bytes per row (an odd width of 3 pixels needs 9 bytes padded to 12).
biXPelsPerMeter = 2835 and biYPelsPerMeter = 5670 (about 72 and 144 dpi): the only metadata a BMP file stores, decoded as ImageMetadata.Resolution without rounding.
The same pixels with a negative biHeight: the first stored row is the top one. Decoding both fixtures to the same reference proves the row order is honored and not merely consistent.
BITMAPV4HEADER with BI_BITFIELDS and an explicit alpha mask: the fourth byte is real transparency, including a fully transparent pixel whose color is still defined and an almost transparent one.

32-bit BI_RGB: the fourth byte holds the same values as bmp/bgra32-v4-alpha but no alpha mask is declared, so it is unspecified padding. The image is the opaque RGB samples; alpha is never guessed from a 32-bit payload.

crossChecks.notes: FFmpeg reads the fourth byte of a 32-bit BI_RGB payload as alpha; the specification leaves it unspecified and no alpha mask is declared, so the reference is opaque. Every color sample agrees exactly (mean color error 0); only the alpha interpretation differs.

reference.description: BITMAPV3INFOHEADER (56 bytes) with a one-bit alpha mask: the single alpha bit expands to 0 or 255, and the color channels keep their defined values under transparent pixels.

crossChecks.notes: FFmpeg expands 5-bit channels by replicating their high bits instead of rounding the exact ratio, and reads this layout as opaque 5-5-5; the alpha bit and the rounding are recorded here.

reference.description: BI_BITFIELDS after a 40-byte BITMAPINFOHEADER: the three masks are stored between the header and the pixel data (and counted in bfOffBits). The green channel is 6 bits wide, the others 5.

crossChecks.notes: FFmpeg expands 5- and 6-bit channels by replicating their high bits instead of rounding the exact ratio; every sample agrees within one unit.

reference.description: Encoded by FFmpeg's independent BMP encoder from the hand-defined pattern; BMP is lossless, so the pattern is the reference.
OS/2 1.x BITMAPCOREHEADER (12 bytes): 16-bit unsigned width and height, planes and bit count, nothing else. The rows are those of bmp/bgr24-bottom-up-padding, always bottom-up.
OS/2 1.x with 1-bit indexes and two RGBTRIPLE entries that are not black and white.

OS/2 1.x with 4-bit indexes: the 16 palette entries are RGBTRIPLE (blue, green, red, three bytes each, no reserved byte), so the pixel data starts at 14 + 12 + 48. Reading four bytes per entry shifts every color.

OS/2 1.x with 8-bit indexes and five palette entries instead of 256, as some files in the wild store: the header has no color count, so the number of entries is what fits before bfOffBits ((42 - 26) / 3 = 5, with one unused byte before the pixel data). An index outside these five entries would be malformed.

The shortest BITMAPCOREHEADER2: 16 bytes, cut after the bit count. Every field it leaves out is zero (uncompressed, a full 16-entry palette, no resolution), and its palette entries are RGBQUAD (four bytes), unlike those of the 12-byte header.

crossChecks.notes: FFmpeg does not decode a BITMAPCOREHEADER2 shorter than 40 bytes.

reference.description: OS/2 2.x BITMAPCOREHEADER2, all 64 bytes: its first 40 bytes are laid out like BITMAPINFOHEADER, and the resolution is in pixels per meter because usUnits is 0 (metric), so it decodes like bmp/bgr24-resolution.

OS/2 2.x 24-bit run-length encoding (compression 4, which a Windows header would read as BI_JPEG): runs of one blue, green, red triplet, an absolute run of three triplets (nine bytes and a padding byte), an absolute run of four triplets (no padding), a delta and an early end of line. There is no palette, so the two skipped pixels are black.

crossChecks.notes: FFmpeg does not decode BCA_RLE24.

reference.description: 1-bit indexes with a two-entry palette that is not black and white: the most significant bit is the left pixel, and the nine pixels of a row occupy two bytes padded to four.
4-bit indexes, odd width: the high nibble is the left pixel, the last byte of each row carries one pixel and one unused nibble, and the row is padded to 4 bytes.

8-bit indexes with a five-entry palette (biClrUsed = 5, not the full 256) and four unused bytes between the palette and the pixel data: bfOffBits is authoritative, the gap is skipped, and the row is padded to 8 bytes.

16-bit BI_RGB: the implicit 5-5-5 masks of the specification. Every channel is expanded to 8 bits with the exact ratio round(value * 255 / 31), so 0 maps to 0 and 31 to 255; two padding bytes follow each 10-byte row.

crossChecks.notes: FFmpeg expands 5-bit channels by replicating their high bits instead of rounding the exact ratio round(value * 255 / 31); every sample agrees within one unit.

reference.description: BI_RLE4 with skipped pixels: a delta that starts a row at its second pixel (an absolute run of three indexes then starts on an odd column and needs no padding byte), an early end of line, a delta that moves three pixels right and one row up, and an end of bitmap that leaves the last stored row unwritten. The skipped pixels are palette index 0, whose color is (200, 100, 50).

BI_RLE4, odd width: a run of four pixels of one index, a run of one pixel (only the high-order index of its byte is used), a run of five pixels alternating two indexes (4, 3, 4, 3, 4), and an absolute run of five indexes stored in three bytes (the last low-order half is unused) followed by its padding byte.

BI_RLE8 with skipped pixels: an end of line after two of six pixels, a delta that moves three pixels right, a delta that moves two pixels right and two rows up (one row is skipped entirely), and an end of bitmap before the end of the fifth stored row, with the sixth never started. The pixels the stream does not store are palette index 0, whose color is (200, 100, 50) here: they are neither black nor transparent.

BI_RLE8, every row complete: encoded runs (a count and one index), an absolute run of four indexes, an absolute run of five indexes followed by its padding byte (absolute runs end on a 16-bit boundary), single pixels stored as runs of one, an end-of-line escape after each row and the end-of-bitmap escape. The stream stores the rows bottom-up.

expectedError.feature: Bit fields: channel wider than 8 bits

fixtures.notes: A 10-10-10-2 bit-field layout: channels wider than 8 bits are recognized and rejected rather than truncated.
The red mask 0x0000F810 is not a contiguous run of bits.
A BITMAPCOREHEADER with bcBitCount 16: OS/2 bitmaps store 1, 4, 8 or 24 bits per pixel.
A 4-bit BITMAPCOREHEADER file whose bfOffBits is 28: two bytes after the 26 bytes of the headers, less than one three-byte palette entry.
An OS/2 2.x header with compression 3, which is CCITT Group 3 one-dimensional (Huffman 1D) coding there, not BI_BITFIELDS: recognized and rejected.
The red and green masks are both 0xF800: the channels of a pixel may not overlap.
A pixel uses the palette index 5, outside the five-entry palette (0 to 4).
bfOffBits is 50, inside the 54-byte header and palette area.
biPlanes is 2; 1 is the only legal value.
A delta moves three rows up from the first of three rows: the current position may not leave the canvas.
BI_RLE8 with biBitCount 4: BI_RLE8 only stores 8-bit indexes (BI_RLE4 stores the 4-bit ones).
A run follows the end of line of the third and last row: only the end-of-bitmap escape may follow the last row.
bmp/rle8-runs-absolute without its last two bytes: every row is complete, but the input ends before the end-of-bitmap escape, so it is truncated.
A run uses the palette index 5, outside the five-entry palette (0 to 4).
A run of three pixels starts at the sixth pixel of a seven-pixel row: a run never wraps to the next row and is never clamped.
BI_RLE8 with a negative biHeight: a run-length encoded bitmap is always bottom-up.
The input ends inside the BITMAPINFOHEADER (after biCompression's first byte).
The input ends five bytes before the end of the last row: truncated input is malformed data, never a clean end of input.
biCompression is 12, which is not a defined BI_* value.
BI_BITFIELDS is declared with a zero green mask.
biHeight is 0; the sign gives the row order and the magnitude the row count.
biWidth is 0; a positive width is required.
Logical screen width 0.
A Graphic Control Extension block of 3 bytes instead of 4, before the first image.
After one literal the next table code is 6: code 7 is not defined (FFmpeg and ImageIO silently decode garbage).
The end code arrives after 2 of the 4 pixels: a short image is an error, never a partial frame.
The first code after a clear code must be a color index: code 6 (KwKwK without a previous code) is invalid.
Minimum code size 12: the clear code would need 13 bits (at most 11 is valid).
The second code (KwKwK) expands to two indices where one pixel remains.
Three indices then the end code for a 2x1 image: more pixels than the rectangle (FFmpeg and ImageIO truncate silently).
The datastream ends without an end code after 2 indices (4 counting the zero padding bits) of a 10-pixel image.
Neither a global nor a local color table (FFmpeg also rejects it; the specification only suggests a system default).
The file ends after the last image without the trailer: truncation, never a clean end.
The trailer follows the loop extension: a GIF needs at least one image.
Index 3 with a 2-entry global color table (FFmpeg shows it transparent, ImageIO as color 0).
Plain text extensions would require text rendering; they are rejected.
Image data sub-blocks and trailer are cut: truncation must be an error, never a clean end of input.
Byte 0x2A after the first image is neither an extension, an image nor the trailer.

crossChecks.decoder: transicc (LittleCMS 2.19) on the inks of the reference
crossChecks.notes: Another color management system on the same inks. The ICC specification does not define the interpolation of a lookup table between its grid points: LittleCMS interpolates a four-dimensional table linearly along its first input and tetrahedrally on the others, the reference multilinearly, so they are several levels apart for some colors: more than the library tolerance of this fixture. The difference bounds an error of table order, encoding or rendering intent, and the tolerance that independent color management systems justify.

comparison.justification: Lossy JPEG compared with an independent decoding of the same encoded input (libjpeg-turbo djpeg: islow integer IDCT), converted by the decimal reference of ICC color conversion. The library decoder (double-precision IDCT rounded to nearest) differs from djpeg by one unit on some ink samples, which the color conversion amplifies where its lookup table is steep; its own conversion is exact with respect to the reference. Measured: max 1, mean 0.0310. Allowed: the measured max and the measured mean + 0.01 (rounded up to 0.01). The policy is verified to reject channel swaps and flips of this reference.

fixtures.notes: CMYK inks (Adobe APP14 transform 0) without profile, progressive: the default progression of libjpeg-turbo for four components. No pixel format holds inks: the file is identified, and loaded only with a color conversion (inkConversion).

crossChecks.notes: swscale stretches the 9x9 chroma planes to 35x9 pixels for odd dimensions instead of centered upsampling by whole factors (error grows across the image): an FFmpeg conversion artifact, not a legitimate decoder difference, so it does not justify the tolerance.

comparison.justification: Lossy JPEG compared with an independent decoding of the same encoded input (libjpeg-turbo djpeg: islow integer IDCT, fancy upsampling). The library decoder (double-precision IDCT rounded to nearest, triangle chroma upsampling with the same edge replication and rounding biases, 16-bit fixed-point JFIF YCbCr->RGB) differs from it only by IDCT rounding, chroma upsampling (4:1:1) (one unit on some component samples, amplified by the color conversion); measured: max 2, mean 0.0402. Allowed: the measured max (at least 1) and the measured mean + 0.01 (rounded up to 0.01), tighter than the disagreement between independent decoders (see reference.crossChecks: max 48, mean 6.3354, which would justify max 49 / mean 9.61). Alpha is compared exactly, and the policy is verified to reject channel swaps and flips of this reference.

reference.description: Encoded by FFmpeg's independent PAM encoder from the hand-defined pattern (RGB_ALPHA); PAM is lossless, so the pattern is the reference.
Plain PBM (P1) with the same pixels as pnm/p4-bitmap-padding: every non-blank character is one pixel and white space is free-form, so both fixtures must decode to the same reference.
Plain PGM (P2) with MAXVAL 15: samples are normalized to the full 8-bit range with the exact ratio round(value * 255 / 15), so 0 stays 0 and 15 becomes 255.
Plain PPM (P3) with MAXVAL 1000: above 255 the samples are 16-bit, normalized with the exact ratio round(value * 65535 / 1000).
Binary PBM (P4) with a header comment: a set bit is black, rows are padded to whole bytes (11 pixels use two bytes and five padding bits) and the single white-space byte after the header ends it.
Binary PGM (P5) with MAXVAL 65535: two big-endian bytes per sample, decoded to Gray16 without losing a bit (the low bytes differ from the high bytes so a byte swap or an 8-bit bottleneck is visible).
Binary PGM (P5) with MAXVAL 255: one byte per sample, decoded to Gray8 unchanged.
Binary PPM (P6) with MAXVAL 65535: the library has no 16-bit RGB pixel format, so the samples are decoded into an opaque Rgba64 without losing a bit.
Binary PPM (P6) with MAXVAL 255: three bytes per pixel in red, green, blue order.
PAM (P7) with TUPLTYPE BLACKANDWHITE and MAXVAL 1: unlike a PBM bit, a PAM sample is an intensity, so 0 is black and 1 is white (the opposite convention of pnm/p4-bitmap-padding).
PAM (P7) with TUPLTYPE GRAYSCALE_ALPHA and DEPTH 2: the library has no gray-with-alpha pixel format, so the gray sample is replicated into red, green and blue, which is lossless.
PAM (P7) with MAXVAL 65535 and TUPLTYPE RGB_ALPHA: 16-bit straight alpha decoded into Rgba64.
PAM (P7) with TUPLTYPE RGB_ALPHA and DEPTH 4: straight alpha, including fully transparent pixels whose colors stay defined.

Assembled chunk by chunk in the generator, each chunk written with the literal pixel it must produce (QOI specification 1.0 semantics, checked by the writer): every opcode, bias extremes, wrap-around, alpha kept by RGB/DIFF/LUMA, an index slot never written (transparent black), the initial pixel's slot after a leading run, runs of 1 and 62 across rows and a run ending the image.

comparison.justification: Lossy VP8 compared with an independent decoding of the same encoded input (libwebp dwebp: RFC 6386 reconstruction, fancy chroma upsampling, 14-bit fixed-point BT.601 YUV->RGB). The library decoder (the same exact VP8 reconstruction, centered bilinear 9-3-3-1 chroma upsampling, 16-bit fixed-point BT.601 conversion rounded to nearest) differs from it only by the rounding of the color conversion; measured: max 1, mean 0.0019. Allowed: the measured max (at least 1) and the measured mean + 0.01 (rounded up to 0.01), tighter than the disagreement between independent decoders (see reference.crossChecks: max 1, mean 0.3333, which would justify max 2 / mean 0.60). Alpha is compared exactly, and the policy is verified to reject channel swaps and flips of this reference.

fixtures.notes: Lossy color with a losslessly compressed alpha plane (ALPH, VP8L image stream with a prediction filter).

av1Vectors.planeDigest: SHA-256 of the samples of one plane of one output frame, film grain applied: rows in order, exactly plane-width samples per row, 1 byte per sample for 8-bit streams and 2 little-endian bytes for 10 and 12-bit streams, no padding. Planes are in bitstream order Y, U, V (planar GBR order G, B, R for an identity-matrix stream), one plane for a monochrome stream; a chroma plane is (width + subsampling_x) >> subsampling_x samples wide and (height + subsampling_y) >> subsampling_y rows high. A digest is recorded only when both decoders produce the same bytes.
